title: The Paxos conduit has only an outbound transferAssets rate limit because its return leg is an off-chain issuer obligation
content:
The USDC To USDG Via Paxos Instance breaks the schema every other Instance follows. A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.15.1.2.3 declares a single identifier — "The **transferAssets** `RateLimitID` for this conduit is `0x4139045d…`" — where other Instances declare an inflow/outflow pair. The identifier field at .15.1.2.1.4 is renamed from "Token" to "**Token to Receive**: USDG." And .15.1.2.2.1 and .15.1.2.2.2 give the Token Address and the Underlying Asset Address as the *same* USDC contract, with the only other address being a "Paxos Deposit Address" (.15.1.2.2.3).

Read together, these describe an operation that is not an on-chain conduit at all: Grove transfers USDC to an address Paxos controls and receives USDG through Paxos's own issuance process. There is no vault, no share token, and nothing on-chain that Grove can call to reverse the transfer.

That explains the missing outflow limit without any special pleading. A rate limit constrains an action Grove can take; the return leg is an action **Paxos** takes. There is nothing on Grove's side to throttle, so the schema's outflow slot has no referent and is simply absent rather than marked "Unlimited" or deferred to a future iteration.

The consequence is worth stating plainly. For this Instance the rate limit is not a risk control on the position — it is a cap on how much unsecured credit Grove can extend to Paxos per day. Once the USDC leaves, Grove holds an obligation, and the 50,000,000 USDC `maxAmount` (.15.1.2.4.1) measures exactly the size of that obligation it can create.

This is where a uniform configuration schema costs the most: an Instance that is economically a counterparty credit exposure is documented in the same shape as one that is a smart-contract position, and the difference shows up only as a missing field.
description: USDC To USDG replaces the usual inflow/outflow pair with a single transferAssets limit and lists identical token and underlying addresses, so the received USDG is secured by counterparty trust
